what_happened.line: The Agricultural Commission put off approving a 2022 farmers market plan until the next meeting; market managers will first poll past vendors.
The proposed plan shortens the season to every other Sunday starting in July, with vendors paying per day instead of a season fee.
No votes were taken. Members were comfortable with managers posting a digital vendor application before the commission formally reviews the plan.
Expanding the commission from five to seven members was moved to ongoing items; members said they want to improve attendance first.
The next meeting was set for March 17.

why_it_matters: The farmers market's schedule and vendor fees for 2022 are still undecided, so anyone who sells at or shops at the market will not know the season's shape until the commission acts.

The plan has vendors pay per-day fees directly to the commission chair rather than to the market manager. Residents who care how town-connected market money is handled may want to see how that is set up.
watch_next: The commission's March 17 meeting, where the farmers market plan is expected to come back after the vendor poll.
